data.statement: Trained and tested on SYNTHETIC scans generated from written-down assumptions. No real attendance or proxy-marking data was used. These numbers describe the method in an invented world, not accuracy on real classes.
assumptions: 8% of scans are proxy marks; the rest are honest.
25% of scans come from lectures with the location check off (location features are then neutral).
30% of scans have a face distance; the rest have none (a 'missing' flag, which carries no label information).
Honest students are 0 to about 150 m from the room centre (half-normal, sigma 35 m); GPS error is a 2-D normal with sigma = accuracy / 2.
Good phone fixes have accuracy near 12 m (lognormal, 3 to 40 m); poor indoor fixes 40 to 150 m, with a tail to 800 m.
Honest students scan at any moment of the code's 55 to 60 s on-screen life (so timing alone says little); at lecture start they scan within 15 s.
A relayed QR photo arrives late in the code's life (beta-shaped, peaking around 35 s) and the relaying student is often outside or in the corridor.
6% of honest students deny location; 30% of proxies do.

Face distance (128-number descriptors): same person about 0.40 +- 0.08, with 4% of honest scans mismatching (glasses, light); a different person about 0.78 +- 0.09. These values are assumptions to be re-measured with real enrolments.
Hard negatives: poor-GPS honest scans, honest lecture-start bursts on shared Wi-Fi, honest shared phones.
The 'second_phone_in_room' proxy is detectable mainly through device history, because their location looks right.

rules_only_baseline.note: The server's rules alone (location grey zone beyond 150 m, imprecise or missing location, a device used by another student), on the same test scans.

rules_and_model_together.note: The server sends a scan to review if the rules OR the model flag it. Most honest scans reviewed here come from the rules (a missing or imprecise location, a phone used by another student).

matched_budget.note: The model given the same share of honest scans sent to review as the rules use. Budget and threshold come from validation data.

development_notes: Logistic regression ships for its readable reasons. Gradient boosting scores higher in this synthetic world (see the benchmark); the gap is the price of explanations.

Extra features (a lecture-start burst indicator, new device x shared device, late-scan curvature, a face distance above 0.55) were tried on the validation split. The best combination gained about 5 points of recall at the 3% cap and none closed the gap, so they were not adopted: gains that small on invented data are as likely to fit the generator as the problem.
Honest students with a new phone or a phone shared with a flatmate are flagged far more often than other honest students (see scenarios). They go to a review queue, never to rejection.
limits: A proxy who is physically in the room and uses a second phone is caught mainly through device history; recall for that scenario is low.
Timing is a weak signal: honest students scan at any moment while a code is on screen.
GPS can be spoofed and a web page cannot detect it; the model only sees what the browser reports.
Face distance has no liveness check, so a photo of a face can pass.
The score is a risk score under the synthetic prior, not the probability that a real student cheated. It only orders scans for a human to review.
